title: Iterated emission machine
statement: Let $G$ and $E$ be finite Turing machines on Boolean words, and let $g,e : \\{0,1\\}^* \\to \\{0,1\\}^*$. Suppose there are natural numbers $C_G,c_G,C_E,c_E$ such that $G$ computes $g$ in time $C_G(n+1)^{c_G}$ and $E$ computes $e$ in time $C_E(n+1)^{c_E}$. If $a',k',b,l$ are natural numbers and every word $w$ and every $i\\ge 0$ satisfy $|g^{i}(w)| \\le b(|w|+1)^l$, then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,c$ such that $M$ computes, in time $C(n+1)^c$, the concatenation of $e(w),e(g(w)),\\ldots,e(g^{a'(|w|+1)^{k'}}(w))$ on input $w$.
hypotheses_covered: $G,E$ are finite Turing machines over Boolean words
$g,e$ are functions from Boolean words to Boolean words
$G$ computes $g$ within $C_G(n+1)^{c_G}$ steps on length-$n$ inputs
$E$ computes $e$ within $C_E(n+1)^{c_E}$ steps on length-$n$ inputs
For every Boolean word $w$ and natural number $i$, $|g^i(w)|\\le b(|w|+1)^l$
